svg.title: Where each of the fourteen tasks stands
svg.desc: The fourteen tasks CTP accepts, in three states. Eight are still CTP's and run as a subprocess with argv and environment reproduced byte for byte: kcc, neis05, neis08, sql_by_cci, jdbc, ha_repl, cdc_repl and webconsole. Five run natively but only when a switch names their family: shell and rqg behind TESTKIT_NATIVE=shell, sql and medium behind TESTKIT_NATIVE=sql, isolation behind TESTKIT_NATIVE=isolation. One, unittest, runs natively with nothing to opt into. A gated task moves right when its comparison against CTP clears and never moves back; unittest is already there and no ADR gates it. The gates: shell and rqg are held by ADR-013, still open, with 3,216 cases judged at develop head and the full-corpus comparison not yet cleared; sql and medium passed ADR-017 with 17,459 result files and 2,762 record files byte-identical to CTP; isolation met ADR-018, with no runner difference at one slot or four, and runs four slots by default, reduced by CPU count and by available memory.
svg.text: Fourteen tasks, three states — and one switch between the second and the third
A gated task moves right when its comparison against CTP clears, and never moves back. unittest is already there: no ADR gates it.
argv and env byte for byte
as CTP would have built them
NATIVE — BUT YOU MUST ASK FOR IT
No switch, no flag. It is
WHAT EACH SWITCH IS WAITING FOR — THE GATE IS WHAT EARNS THE MOVE RIGHT
3,216 cases judged at develop head, every one of the 32 failures attributed.
The full-corpus comparison has not cleared. That is the gate.
17,459 .result and 2,762 record files byte-identical to a clean CTP run.
No runner difference at one slot or at four; four slots by default, fewer on a small machine.
CTP does not reproduce its own verdicts here: two CTP runs disagree on 7 of 6,772.
Seven further names — cci · dots · nbd · sysbench · tpcc · tpcw · ycsb — are ones CTP accepted and silently ignored.
They now say they are retired, and the next task still runs.
